title: Preliminary validation of a newly developed Spanish-language patient-perceived scale of LGB clinical competence and sensitivity in psychotherapy
abstract: Abstract Lesbian, gay, and bisexual (LGB) people face minority stress that can also shape their experience of psychotherapy. Their perceptions of therapists’ attitudes and competence are associated with satisfaction and the therapeutic alliance, yet few instruments assess these perceptions from the patient’s perspective. This cross-sectional study aimed to develop and provide initial psychometric evidence for a Spanish-language Patient-Perceived LGB Clinical Competence and Sensitivity Scale (ECCS-LGB-P) to assess LGB patients’ perceptions of their therapists’ clinical competence and sensitivity. Data were collected from 203 Spanish-speaking LGB adults. Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) yielded a provisional two-factor structure (Sensitivity and Positive Clinical Competence; Microaggressions and Discriminatory Practices) that largely coincided with positive versus negative item wording. The final 30-item scale showed high internal consistency ( $$\alpha = .96$$ ; McDonald’s $$\omega = .96$$ ), which may partly reflect item redundancy. ECCS-LGB-P scores were moderately associated with patients’ ratings of the therapeutic alliance ( $$\rho = .55$$ , $$p < .001$$ ). No statistically reliable associations were detected with symptom measures. These findings provide promising preliminary evidence concerning the internal structure, internal consistency, and relations with the therapeutic alliance of the ECCS-LGB-P, mainly for research, training, and group-level quality improvement. Confirmatory factor analysis, measurement invariance testing, and test–retest reliability in independent samples are needed before broad implementation.
